quotes.why: Tsongkhapa reports the seventeen Mother-and-Sons as the earlier masters' convention — the position p4 opens with. Found by direct search.
The same five omitted sūtras that p4 uses for its first fault, with Tsongkhapa's endorsement of the objection. Found by direct search.
Tsongkhapa's second fault, which p4 states without his sharpness — counting the Saṃcayagāthā separately shows one has not seen the volume. Found by direct search.
The chapter count on which p4's second fault turns, in its source. Found by direct search.
Tsongkhapa refuses the ninefold scheme on the same ground p4 gives — this is what རིགས་པ་སྔ་མས་ཁེགས་སོ points to. Found by direct search.
Tsongkhapa's own criterion for a root sūtra, from which he reaches four or five — not the three p5 will hold. Found by direct search.
What the སྡུད་འགྲེལ actually says at the place p4's objector cites; the yig cha's wording is a paraphrase, not a quotation. Found by direct search.
Haribhadra's gloss of the very line p4's objector quotes: the four assemblies had already trained on the extensive text. Found by direct search.
The same citation put to different work in the companion volume — evidence of what Chökyi Gyaltsen takes it to establish. Found by direct search.
Gomang reaches the three-Mother position p5 will state, and on Haribhadra's authority rather than by refuting counts. Found by direct search.
